name: Question 3
problem:
Given that the differential equation

$$
{y}^{″}+2{y}^{′}+17y=0
$$

has the general solution

$$
y={e}^{-x}(P\operatorname{cos}⁡4x+Q\operatorname{sin}⁡4x),
$$

solve the initial value problem

$$
{y}^{″}+2{y}^{′}+17y=0,\,y(0)=-1,\,{y}^{′}(0)=-11.
$$
worked_solution:
We find the constants $P$ and $Q$ using the initial conditions. 

- Substituting $y(0)=-1$ into the general solution gives

$$
P=-1.
$$

- To apply the condition ${y}^{′}(0)=-11,$ we first differentiate $y$ to get

$$
{y}^{′}=-{e}^{-x}(P\operatorname{cos}⁡4x+Q\operatorname{sin}⁡4x)+{e}^{-x}(-4P\operatorname{sin}⁡4x+4Q\operatorname{cos}⁡4x).
$$

Then, we substitute ${y}^{′}(0)=-11$ into the above to get

$$
-P+4Q=-11.
$$

Using the fact that $P=-1$ gives $Q=-3.$

Therefore, the solution to the initial value problem is

$$
\begin{aligned}y & ={e}^{-x}(-\operatorname{cos}⁡4x-3\operatorname{sin}⁡4x).\end{aligned}
$$

Question 3
?

Given that the differential equation y″+2y′+17y=0 has the general solution y=e−x(Pcos⁡4x+Qsin⁡4x), solve the initial value problem y″+2y′+17y=0,y(0)=−1,y′(0)=−11.

a
y=e−x(−cos⁡4x+2sin⁡4x)
b
y=e−x(−cos⁡4x−4sin⁡4x)
c
y=e−x(−cos⁡4x+5sin⁡4x)
d
y=e−x(−cos⁡4x−sin⁡4x)
e
y=e−x(−cos⁡4x−3sin⁡4x)
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

We find the constants P and Q using the initial conditions.

  • Substituting y(0)=−1 into the general solution gives P=−1.

  • To apply the condition y′(0)=−11, we first differentiate y to get y′=−e−x(Pcos⁡4x+Qsin⁡4x)+e−x(−4Psin⁡4x+4Qcos⁡4x). Then, we substitute y′(0)=−11 into the above to get −P+4Q=−11. Using the fact that P=−1 gives Q=−3.

Therefore, the solution to the initial value problem is y=e−x(−cos⁡4x−3sin⁡4x).
